sections.html: Family: Ariidae. Size: 55 cm total length. Climate: subtropical, 41°N – 28°S. IUCN Red List: Not Evaluated.
Africa: widely distributed in southern Africa; in freshwater, estuaries and coastal environments. Type locality: around Cape Town [South Africa].
Generally found in large shoals on muddy bottoms in turbid waters, usually on the coastline and in estuaries. Also found in rivers.
Feeds on crayfish, small fish and crabs.
Dimorphism of the posterior (humeral) process of the cleithrum is obvious externally: fan-shaped in females, triangular in males. The maxillary barbel is longer in females.

Description: vertebrae 51–52 (17 precaudal, 34–35 caudal). Head longer than, or nearly as long as, broad; relatively long and thin maxillary barbel, extending at least to the pectoral fin spine origin; deeply forked caudal fin with pointed lobes, the upper lobe longer; 11–14 gill rakers on the anterior face of the first arch; 10–12 pectoral fin rays; upper two-thirds of the body darkened, with some lateral speckling and a stark white belly.

Etymology: the specific name feliceps comes from felis, cat, and ceps, head, i.e. "cathead", a variation on the term "catfish", referring to the cat-like whiskers (barbels).

Remarks: considered a nuisance by shore and ski-boat anglers in southern Africa as little else is caught. The spines are poisonous and wounds should be treated immediately.
